newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian fuel scarcity hits oil stocks.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian fuel scarcity hits oil stocks.

text.p: A two-week-old fuel scarcity took the shine off the shares of oil marketing firms on the Nigerian bourse on Friday, taking down with it the all-share index.
The index slipped to 8667.62 from 8667.64 on Thursday.
Traders said the oil shares would continue to slide next week over the fuel scarcity but also because some of them had become overpriced.
Agip was the first casualty on Friday, falling to 27.35 naira, down five kobo.
"For many months, dealers have been raising prices without recourse to the fundamentals," said one trader.
Unipetrol, the market's dearest stock, managed to end unchanged at 76.10 naira.
Oil shares have not moved for the two weeks since fuel queues started forming at petrol stations because of production and distribution problems.
Dealers said unless the situation improved next week, investors might panic and sell oil company shares, usually hard to find in the market.
"There is the possibility that investors would choose to sell and benefit from their current high prices than see them begin to weaken," a trader said.
Conglomerates were Friday's top performers on increasingly good prospects. Market watchers said they expected good full year results from UAC and Lever Brothers soon.
UAC rose by 82 kobo, the maximum five percent allowed daily, to close at 17.22 naira. Lever Brothers rose 30 kobo to 27.60 naira while PZ Industries soared 60 kobo to 28.20 naira.
Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company was up 30 kobo at 52.80 naira on increasing demand and Nestle gained 10 kobo at 68.30 naira.
Most bank shares were quiet on Friday but Afribank and UBA finished 35 kobo and 10 higher, respectively. Afribank ended at 9.90 naira and UBA at 14.40 naira.
Friday's other loser was Trade Bank which went ex-scrip at 1.40 naira, shedding 70 kobo.
